package proto

import (
	"runtime"
	"runtime/debug"
	"syscall"
	"testing"
	"unsafe"
)

// These tests make the generated code fail on purpose: a read and a write
// through an address that is mapped to nothing, a store into the guard page
// above the shadow stack, and a trap. The Go runtime ends the process for
// each of them unless the host turned on SetPanicOnFault (the first three) or
// the generated code calls host_trap in place of a trap instruction (the
// last). Each must be a panic that recovers, with the process, the other VMs
// and a new VM as they were. They run on linux/amd64 and darwin/arm64.

// fails runs f as an entry into the code with SetPanicOnFault on, as the host
// of the engine does (gohost.Enter), and returns what it panicked with. A
// panic that leaves through the code breaks the VM.
func fails(vm *VM, f func(sp uintptr) int64) (got any) {
	defer func() {
		if got = recover(); got != nil {
			vm.broken = true
		}
	}()
	defer debug.SetPanicOnFault(debug.SetPanicOnFault(true))
	vm.Eval(f)
	return nil
}

func wantFault(t *testing.T, got any, what string, lo, hi uintptr) {
	t.Helper()
	if got == nil {
		t.Fatalf("%s: the code did not fail", what)
	}
	if _, ok := got.(runtime.Error); !ok {
		t.Fatalf("%s: panicked with %T %v, want a runtime.Error", what, got, got)
	}
	a, ok := got.(interface{ Addr() uintptr })
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("%s: the panic %v names no address", what, got)
	}
	if hi != 0 && (a.Addr() < lo || a.Addr() >= hi) {
		t.Fatalf("%s: the fault is at %#x, want %#x to %#x", what, a.Addr(), lo, hi)
	}
}

// afterFailure checks that a VM that failed refuses to run, that closing it
// is fine, that the goroutine has its setting of SetPanicOnFault back, and
// that a new VM runs the generated code.
func afterFailure(t *testing.T, vm *VM, what string) {
	t.Helper()
	if _, err := vm.Eval(func(sp uintptr) int64 { return rec(sp, 3) }); err != ErrBroken {
		t.Errorf("%s: Eval after the failure gave %v, want ErrBroken", what, err)
	}
	vm.Close()
	if debug.SetPanicOnFault(false) {
		t.Errorf("%s: the goroutine still has SetPanicOnFault on", what)
	}
	w := NewVM()
	defer w.Close()
	if r, err := w.Eval(func(sp uintptr) int64 { return rec(sp, 100) }); err != nil || r != 5050 {
		t.Errorf("%s: a new VM gave %d, %v", what, r, err)
	}
}

func TestFaultWildPointer(t *testing.T) {
	wilds := []uintptr{0xdead0000, 0x10000, 1 << 46, 0xdeadbeefdeadbeef}
	for _, wild := range wilds {
		for _, c := range []struct {
			name string
			do   func(sp uintptr) int64
		}{
			{"read", func(sp uintptr) int64 { return peek(sp, wild) }},
			{"write", func(sp uintptr) int64 { return poke(sp, wild, 7) }},
		} {
			t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
				vm := NewVM()
				got := fails(vm, c.do)
				// A non-canonical address has no address to report on amd64.
				lo, hi := wild, wild+1<<20
				if wild == 0xdeadbeefdeadbeef && runtime.GOARCH == "amd64" {
					lo, hi = 0, 0
				}
				wantFault(t, got, c.name, lo, hi)
				afterFailure(t, vm, c.name)
			})
		}
	}
}

// TestFaultDivide: x86 raises a divide error for a division by zero, and the
// Go runtime turns that signal into a panic whatever the setting. arm64 has no
// such fault: the division gives 0.
func TestFaultDivide(t *testing.T) {
	if runtime.GOARCH != "amd64" {
		vm := NewVM()
		defer vm.Close()
		if r, err := vm.Eval(func(sp uintptr) int64 { return quot(sp, 7, 0) }); err != nil || r != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("7 / 0 gave %d, %v on %s, want 0", r, err, runtime.GOARCH)
		}
		return
	}
	vm := NewVM()
	got := fails(vm, func(sp uintptr) int64 { return quot(sp, 7, 0) })
	if err, ok := got.(runtime.Error); !ok || err.Error() != "runtime error: integer divide by zero" {
		t.Fatalf("a division by zero panicked with %T %v, want the runtime's integer divide by zero", got, got)
	}
	afterFailure(t, vm, "a division by zero")
}

// TestFaultGuardPage: the stack has all but 8 bytes in use, and the stores of
// a frame go into the page above it, which is mapped to nothing.
func TestFaultGuardPage(t *testing.T) {
	vm := NewVM()
	end := vm.base + shadowSize
	pg := uintptr(syscall.Getpagesize())
	off := end - uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(&vm.mem[0]))
	if err := syscall.Mprotect(vm.mem[off:off+pg], syscall.PROT_NONE); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	got := fails(vm, func(sp uintptr) int64 { return hit_end(end - 8) })
	wantFault(t, got, "an entry with no stack left", end, end+pg)
	afterFailure(t, vm, "the guard page")
}

// TestFaultTrap: the C traps. In Go a ud2 or a brk is SIGILL or SIGTRAP, which
// end the process; the pass calls host_trap instead, and it panics.
func TestFaultTrap(t *testing.T) {
	vm := NewVM()
	got := fails(vm, func(sp uintptr) int64 { return trap_now(sp, 1) })
	if got != "host_trap" {
		t.Fatalf("the trap panicked with %T %v, want host_trap", got, got)
	}
	afterFailure(t, vm, "a trap")
}
